column1: # Constellation Arabic Engine — M5 regression corpus.
# This file is the authoritative snapshot of the analyzer's expected
# behaviour across ~500 representative surfaces. Loaded via `include_str!`
# at compile time; parsed and run by the harness in `regression.rs`.
#   The unit tests in `mod.rs::tests` cover flagship cases (وائل,
#   الأئمة, الكاتب). This corpus is the broader safety net — a change
#   that silently alters analyzer behaviour on one narrow pattern shows
#   up as concrete failing rows, not as an end-user complaint months
#   surface  — the raw input passed to `arabic::analyze_best`.
#                generative → hit the generative FST (Layer 3 or 3b).
#                heuristic  → fell through to the low-confidence
#                foreign    → non-Arabic script, routed via Layer 1 +
#                             Layer 4 with Foreign POS. Mapped to
#   lemma    — expected `Analysis.lemma`, or `-` to skip the assertion.
#              Use `-` for ambiguous generative hits where the top
#              analysis is not stable across refactors.
#              or `-` for root-less origins (protected, foreign) or
#              where the specific root is not being asserted.
#   The corpus is pass/fail; there is no confidence-threshold knob.
#   If a case starts failing, either the analyzer regressed (bug) or
#   the row needs an updated expectation (drift). Either way, a human
#   reviews it — silent drift is the whole failure mode the corpus
#   - Append new cases at the bottom of the relevant section.
#   - When the analyzer's behaviour intentionally changes (e.g. a new
#     affix is added), update the affected rows in the same commit that
#   - Never delete a case without documenting why in the commit message.
# § 1 — Protected layer. Hash-lookup on the tashkeel-stripped surface.
# All 250 rows below are drawn from `protected_seed.tsv` (~1,200 total
# entries; sampled here across all four categories).
# § 2 — Generative bare hits. The surface is a direct (root × pattern)
# derivation; the FST returns a match on exact stripped lookup. Root
# assertions are specific; lemma is usually left as `-` because the
# generator may emit several close variants for some patterns and
# Note: حامد / محمود / حمد are also common Arabic given names, so they
# land in the protected list — `analyze_best` returns origin=protected.
# The corpus captures that contract; if a future refactor reorders the
# layers and the root analysis starts winning, these rows will fail and
# force a human review. يحمد (imperfect "he praises") is not a name, so
# it still exercises the generative path.
# Note: حافظ is a common Arabic given name → protected list wins.
# Note: شاكر is a common Arabic given name → protected list wins.
# Note: ناصر and منصور are both very common Arabic given names →
# protected list wins. ناصر is already covered by its protected-section
# row (around line 136), so we don't repeat it here — duplicates would
# mask regressions by shadowing earlier rows in the diagnostic report.
# § 3 — Cascade (affix-stripping) hits. Bare generative lookup misses;
# the analyzer peels legal prefix/suffix chains, looks the stem up,
# and returns the analysis annotated with the peeled affixes. Root
# assertions still hold because peeling does not change the root — it
# only surfaces the clitics that wrapped it.
# ── § 3.1 — Definite article ال + derivations of ك-ت-ب ────────────────
# ── § 3.2 — Definite article ال + derivations of ع-ل-م / ع-م-ل ──────
# ── § 3.3 — Definite article ال + other active participles ────────────
# ── § 3.8 — Chained prefixes (و + ب + ال, ف + ب + ال) ─────────────────
# ── § 3.9 — The M2.b flagship: broken plural through cascade ──────────
# الأئمة decomposes via ال + أئمة (broken plural of إمام, root ء-م-م).
# This is the case that the whole fifth-layer architecture was built for.
# § 4 — Foreign (non-Arabic script). The normalizer routes Latin /
# Hebrew / other scripts through the bypass with Foreign POS at
# the `foreign` sentinel in this TSV maps to it for readability.
